meta.titre: Multimedia File Formats: extensions, categories and free space on a drive
meta.sous_theme: File extensions and sizes of picture, sound, video and document files

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A young photographer in Kribi stores wedding photos, songs and video clips on one flash drive and one day the drive is full. To choose what to delete, she looks at the end of each file name: .jpg, .mp3, .mp4, .docx. Those few letters tell her the kind of file and the program that opens it. The GCE asks you to classify files by extension, to explain what the extension means, and to calculate how much space remains on a storage device.

items: A file has a name followed by a dot and an extension.
1 byte holds one character; KB, MB and GB are larger units of storage.
Pictures, sound and video can all be stored as computer files.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### The file extension

The **file extension** is the group of characters after the last dot in a file name, for example `.jpg`. It shows the **format** (the way the data is organised) and tells the operating system **which program should open** the file.

### Common formats

| Category | Common extensions | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Picture (image) | JPEG or JPG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | JPEG is compressed for photographs; GIF supports simple animation and few colours; BMP is usually uncompressed |
| Sound (audio) | MP3, WAV, WMA, MIDI | MP3 is compressed; WAV is usually uncompressed and large |
| Video | MP4, AVI, MPEG, WMV, MOV | Video is large because it holds many pictures and sound |
| Document | DOC and DOCX, TXT, PDF, XLS and XLSX, PPT | TXT holds plain text only |

### Compression

**Compression** reduces file size. **Lossy** compression throws away some detail that is hard to notice (JPEG, MP3), so the file is much smaller but the original cannot be recovered exactly. **Lossless** compression keeps all the data (PNG, ZIP).

### Storage units and free space

1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB, 1 GB = 1024 MB.

To find the **free space** on a device:

1. Convert every size to the same unit (usually MB).
2. Add the sizes of all the files.
3. Subtract the total from the capacity of the device.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a list of file names is given.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Look only at the extension. Say "likely" because an extension can be changed by the user. Group each file into picture, sound, video or document and, for full marks, name the extension and its significance (the file type and the program that opens it).

variantes.quand_utiliser: When files are given in KB and MB.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Divide by 1024 to go up a unit (KB to MB) and multiply by 1024 to go down (GB to MB). For example 512 KB / 1024 = 0.5 MB.

sections.enonce_markdown: A 4 GB flash drive holds: photo.jpg (3 MB), holiday.mp4 (180 MB), song.mp3 (6 MB), notes.docx (512 KB) and logo.png (2 MB). (a) Classify each file. (b) Calculate the free space in MB, taking the whole 4 GB as usable.

etapes.resultat_markdown: jpg: picture. mp4: video. mp3: sound. docx: document. png: picture.

etapes.justification: All sizes must be in MB.
Free space = capacity minus used space.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **photo.jpg and logo.png are pictures, holiday.mp4 is video, song.mp3 is sound, notes.docx is a document. Free space = 3904.5 MB.** In a real drive the usable capacity is slightly less than the stated one.

items.erreur_markdown: Adding 512 KB directly to sizes in MB (3 + 180 + 6 + 512 + 2).
items.pourquoi_faux: The units are different, so the total is meaningless.

items.erreur_markdown: Converting 4 GB to MB as 4 x 100 = 400 MB.

items.pourquoi_faux: MP3 stores compressed sound only; video formats include MP4, AVI and MPEG.

items.erreur_markdown: "Lossy compression keeps every detail of the original."
items.pourquoi_faux: Lossy compression removes some data permanently; lossless compression keeps all of it.
items.correction_markdown: JPEG and MP3 are lossy; PNG and ZIP are lossless.

items.enonce_markdown: Classify each as picture, sound, video or document: (a) .jpg, (b) .mp3, (c) .avi, (d) .docx.

(a) State what the characters after the dot in a file name are called and their significance. (b) Convert 3072 KB to MB and 2.5 GB to MB. (c) Why is a WAV song usually larger than an MP3 of the same song?
items.solution_markdown: (a) The **file extension**; it shows the format of the file and which program should open it. (b) 3072 / 1024 = **3 MB**; 2.5 x 1024 = **2560 MB**. (c) WAV is usually stored uncompressed, while MP3 uses lossy compression that removes details, so it is much smaller.

items.enonce_markdown: An 8 GB flash drive holds 3 songs of 5 MB each, 2 videos of 700 MB each, 120 photos of 2 MB each and one document of 1536 KB. (a) Calculate the free space in MB. (b) How many more 700 MB videos can be added?
items.solution_markdown: (a) Capacity 8 x 1024 = 8192 MB. Songs 3 x 5 = 15 MB; videos 2 x 700 = 1400 MB; photos 120 x 2 = 240 MB; document 1536 / 1024 = 1.5 MB. Used: 15 + 1400 + 240 + 1.5 = 1656.5 MB. Free: 8192 - 1656.5 = **6535.5 MB**. (b) 6535.5 / 700 = 9.34, so **9 more videos** (the part of a video does not count).

items_markdown: The file extension (the characters after the dot) shows the format and the program that opens the file.
Pictures: JPG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF; sound: MP3, WAV; video: MP4, AVI, MPEG; documents: DOCX, TXT, PDF.
Lossy compression (JPEG, MP3) makes files smaller by removing detail; lossless (PNG, ZIP) keeps all data.
1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB, 1 GB = 1024 MB.
Free space = capacity minus the total of the file sizes, all in the same unit.
